page: Amazon Web Services h1.4xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by the Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 16 vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, alongside a 45 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is allocated at 64 GB, offering a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Network throughput is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

A key characteristic of this instance is the inclusion of 4,000 GB of local magnetic hard disk drive (HDD) storage. Unlike NVMe-backed configurations designed for random IOPS, this local HDD tier is structured to handle sequential data streams and large block transfers. Graphics processing units are absent from this configuration, concentrating system resources strictly on compute, memory, and high-density disk volume.

Benchmark evaluations reflect the architectural age of the Broadwell-era Xeon CPU. Single-core processing is limited, with Geekbench single-core recording 904.0 points and stress-ng single-core reaching 885.2, both falling in the bottom decile of comparative hardware. Multi-core performance scales predictably across the 16 virtual threads, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 16,151.79 and Geekbench multi-core of 5,570.0. Memory write throughput on large blocks registers at a modest 24.12 GB/sec, while in-memory operations like Redis SET achieve 4.91 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides economical bulk storage density relative to solid-state alternatives. The primary operational tradeoff is subdued single-thread execution and elevated disk latency inherent to magnetic media. As a result, the h1.4xlarge is best suited for big data processing clusters, sequential data ingestion, distributed file systems, batch log analytics, and archival data workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services h1.4xlarge is a storage-optimized instance configured with 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor running at 2.3 GHz. It incorporates 64 GB of system memory, 5 Gbps baseline network performance, and 4,000 GB of dedicated local HDD storage. Deployed on the Xen hypervisor without discrete GPU acceleration, the platform delivers moderate multi-threaded compute, indicated by a PassMark CPU score of 16,151.79 and Geekbench multi-core score of 5,570.0. Single-core performance and uncached memory write speeds remain comparatively modest, reflecting the older CPU generation. Cost efficiency is driven primarily by the high capacity of bundled magnetic storage rather than raw computation. Consequently, this server is suitable for large-volume sequential processing, batch data warehousing, distributed file storage, and data-intensive ETL pipelines.
